body.statement:
Let \(F:X\to\mathbb R^d\) be continuously differentiable on a compact box \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\), let \(x\in X\), let \(C\) be nonsingular, and let \(\boldsymbol J_F(X)\) enclose every Jacobian on \(X\).  If
\[
x-CF(x)+\{I-C A:A\in\boldsymbol J_F(X)\}(X-x)
\subset\operatorname{int}(X),
\]
then \(F\) has a zero in \(X\).

source.locator: Nonlinear-equation verification discussion of the Krawczyk operator
source.verbatim_statement: If S(X,x̃) ⊆ int(X), then the preconditioner and enclosed Jacobians are nonsingular, and there is a unique root in x̃+S(X,x̃).
